about: The state log's entry points (docs/log.md), per ENGINE FAMILY. `globals` are top-level functions (hooked as properties of the global object, where the game declares them as functions); `layer` paths are relative to EVERY layer — `layers[<l>]` and its `tmp[<l>]` copy — with `*` matching any key, so a path matches nothing in a game that does not have it. A family `extends` another and adds to both lists; a game belongs to the family whose `members` name it, else to `default`. Census (log-1, 2026-09-30, every game on the roster): the globals are writable functions in 175/175 games (buyUpgrade 172: 2 absent, 1 a lexical `let`; unlockUpg 4; clickGrid 158; resetRow where declared); the non-global click targets are from a `v-on:click` / `@click` / `onclick` census over each game's components.js, systemComponents.js and index.html.

tmt.about: Every engine. `run(tmp[layer].buyables[data].sellOne, …)` on 2.6+ (163 games) and `tmp[layer].buyables[data].sellOne()` on the 2.2.1 PTR engines call the same function; the master button likewise.

ptr.about: Prestige Tree Rewritten's 2.2.1 engine and the games built on it: pseudo-upgrades (`unlockUpg`, a global), Mastery (`layers.ma.startMastery(layer)` from a tree node, `layers.ma.completeMastery(layer)` from a button) and a tree node's own `layers[layer].onClick()`.

arctree.about: Arc Tree's Awakening buttons (`layers.awaken.startAwake(layer)`, `layers.awaken.completeAwake(layer)`), the same shape as PTR's Mastery.
